newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open down on rate worries, dollar.
newsitem.headline: French shares open down on rate worries, dollar.

text.p: French shares opened lower on Tuesday, pressured by a fall in the dollar and bond prices and concerns about the direction of European interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 21.10 points or 0.98 percent at 2,129.29 points -- an important support -- at 0850 GMT. The CAC futures contract was down 18.50 points at 2,130.
The bourse followed bonds lower on a report from six German economic institutes that said monetary policy may be tightened if M3 money supply growth remained strong.

A trader said the market's weakness was exacerbated by thin volume. "The European markets are cautious because we'll be closed on Friday when a lot of important U.S. economic data will be coming out," he said.
Brokers said investors are also unnerved by the public outcry over the French government's Thomson privatisation.
Shares in the Lagardere group, whose bid is favoured by the government, were 0.3 percent lower at 154 francs after tumbling five percent on Monday.

Drinks groups rose against the trend after cognac firm Remy Cointreau reported a four percent rise in first-half sales. Remy shares were up nearly two percent at 128.60 francs. Pernod Ricard shares gained 2.3 percent to 275 francs, helped by a campaign to challenge a proposed increase in spirits taxes.
